summary: This paper studies quantum heavy-tailed multi-armed bandits and stochastic linear bandits with a quantum reward oracle. It proposes QTME, which achieves mean-estimation error ~O(n^{-2v/(1+v)}) up to logs, and derives regret bounds of O(u^{1/(1+v)} K T^{(1-v)/(1+v)} log T) for QMAB and O(d^2 u^{1/(1+v)} T^{(1-v)/(1+v)} polylog(T)) for QSLB. The experiments are simulation-based and compare Heavy-QUCB against robust UCB and Heavy-QLinUCB against LinUCB, with no named quantum hardware reported.

experiments.description: Quantum multi-armed bandit (QMAB) heavy-tailed reward experiment comparing Heavy-QUCB against classical robust UCB on synthetic Pareto-distributed rewards for three instances (S1, S2, S3) with K=5 arms and two heavy-tail settings v=0.5 and v=0.2.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Truncated Mean Estimator (QTME) inside Heavy-QUCB; phased UCB with doubling trick

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Quantum reward oracle O_i encodes the reward distribution of arm i; QTME estimates arm means from oracle access rather than observed samples.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize cumulative regret R_T = T mu* - E[sum_t x_t]

problem_instance.description: Synthetic heavy-tailed MAB with 5 arms and three mean-gap instances S1, S2, S3; rewards sampled from Pareto distributions with shape alpha and arm-specific scale lambda_i.

dataset_specification.description: K=5; S1 means {0.1,0.3,0.5,0.7,0.9}; S2 quadratic convex means mu_a = 0.05(a-5)^2 + 0.1; S3 concave means mu_a = -0.05(a-1)^2 + 0.9; 100 repetitions; T=10^6

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Repeated 100 times; average regret and standard deviation reported; comparison against robust UCB.

speedup_claims.factor: polynomial improvement; factor of O(T^(v/(1+v))) over classical heavy-tailed MAB regret
speedup_claims.conditions: heavy-tailed rewards with bounded (1+v)-th raw moment; quantum reward oracle; regret bound stated for Heavy-QUCB
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports a theoretical regret improvement; experiments are simulations and the paper does not provide exact numeric regret values in text for the plotted curves.

speedup_claims.factor: quadratic improvement in mean estimation error: O(n^(-2v/(1+v))) vs O(n^(-v/(1+v)))
speedup_claims.conditions: heavy-tailed distributions with bounded (1+v)-th raw moment
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a theoretical oracle-query complexity result, not a hardware benchmark.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(K T^{(1-v)/(1+v)} log T) regret; QTME mean estimation error ~ O(n^{-2v/(1+v)}) up to logs
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O((K log T)^{v/(1+v)} T^{1/(1+v)}) regret for heavy-tailed MAB

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Would require a fault-tolerant implementation of QTME/QMAB; the paper reports only simulation-based results and no hardware resource counts.
limiting_factors: no device or qubit count reported
no circuit depth or gate counts reported
advantage is theoretical regret improvement, not an experimental hardware advantage

notes: Hardware is not tied to a named QPU; experiments are described as simulations of the quantum mean estimator and bandit algorithms, so simulator_other is inferred.
The paper reports no explicit qubit count or circuit depth for the QMAB experiment; num_qubits and circuit_depth remain null.
The paper reports improved regret bounds and simulation results, but no real hardware benchmark or practical quantum advantage demonstration.

experiments.description: Quantum stochastic linear bandit (QSLB) heavy-tailed reward experiment comparing Heavy-QLinUCB against classical LinUCB on a finite 2D action set with three theta* instances and synthetic heavy-tailed rewards.

algorithm.variant: Heavy-QLinUCB with QTME and weighted least squares; implicit doubling trick

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Quantum reward oracle O_i encodes reward distributions for selected actions; QTME estimates action rewards used in weighted least squares.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Minimize cumulative regret R(T) = sum_t (a* - a_t)^T theta*

problem_instance.description: Synthetic 2D stochastic linear bandit with 50 actions equally spaced on the positive part of the unit circle and three theta* instances.

dataset_specification.description: Finite action set of 50 unit-circle actions; theta* instances as specified; 100 repetitions; T=10^6

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Repeated 100 times; average regret and standard deviation reported; compared with LinUCB; appendix also compares with QLinUCB from prior work.

speedup_claims.factor: polynomial improvement; factor of ~O(T^(v/(1+v))) over classical heavy-tailed SLB regret
speedup_claims.conditions: heavy-tailed rewards with bounded (1+v)-th raw moment; quantum reward oracle; v in [1/3, 1] for the stated theorem
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports a theoretical regret improvement and a simulation comparison against LinUCB, but no exact numeric regret values are given in the text for the figure.

speedup_claims.factor: improves on classical heavy-tailed SLB by a factor of ~O(T^(v/(1+v)))
speedup_claims.conditions: infinite-arm SLB setting; theorem stated for v in [1/3, 1]
speedup_claims.caveats: This is an asymptotic claim; the appendix figure only shows qualitative lower regret for Heavy-QLinUCB.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(d^2 T^{(1-v)/(1+v)} polylog(T)) regret; QTME mean estimation error ~ O(n^{-2v/(1+v)}) up to logs
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(d T^{1/(1+v)}) regret for heavy-tailed SLB

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Would require a fault-tolerant implementation of Heavy-QLinUCB/QTME; the paper reports only simulation-based results and no hardware resource counts.
limiting_factors: no device or qubit count reported

advantage is theoretical regret improvement, not an experimental hardware advantage
